meaning: compression does not make these detectors forget unseen attack families; the off-distribution method route is closed on this setup, and method effort moves to a problem that is open

prereg.question: does a pruned and recovered CICIoT2023 detector raise an attack family it never saw in training less often than the dense detector trained and recovered the same way, at matched in-distribution risk
prereg.motivation: notebook 40: up to 90% realised FLOP reduction costs nothing in deployed risk after two full epochs of recovery, so no pruning method has anything to win in distribution; recovery cannot help on traffic absent from the training data, and compressed models are known to lose rare and atypical inputs while keeping aggregate accuracy; the locked test partition already showed the shallow students losing 0.06-0.13 fine macro-F1 against the teacher's 0.03; this notebook measures the unseen-family gap before any method is designed

design.corpus: CICIoT2023, frozen split, validation only (no test access); evaluation subsample of notebooks 37-40 (up to 4,000 rows per class, seed 0)
design.held_out_rule: every class of the held-out family is removed from the training rows, the class weights, the clipping bounds, the recalibration slice and the Fisher batches; the models have one output per remaining class; the in-distribution audit uses the evaluation rows of the remaining classes; the unseen audit uses the evaluation rows of the held-out family; one thing is shared across settings and not refit per family: the frozen bridge's per-feature standardisation (mean and standard deviation of the full training split), which carries no label information
design.architectures: shallow CNN (64/128) and deep CNN (64/128/128/256), one output per remaining class
design.teacher: trained from scratch per (architecture, family, seed): 4 epochs, Adam 1e-3, batch 1,024, inverse-square-root class weights normalised to unit mean, seeded initialisation and shuffle, inputs clipped at the 0.1 and 99.9 percentiles of 400,000 remaining training rows (seed 2026)
design.teacher_acceptance: on the remaining classes' evaluation rows, after recalibration: benign escalation at most 0.10, attack recall at least 0.85, fine macro-F1 at least 0.40 (looser than notebook 29's 0.90 and 0.50 because holding out a family removes some of the easiest classes from the pooled recall and the mean); the rule exists to exclude a broken teacher, not to select a good one; a cell whose teacher fails is excluded from the verdict and listed
design.dense_reference: the cell's teacher given two further epochs under the cell's recovery seed, then recalibrated (same treatment as the students)
design.students: magnitude (L1) and Fisher scores computed on the teacher (Fisher on 40 training batches of remaining classes); removal orders ascending with per-layer floors (shallow 4, deep 8); prefixes calibrated to 70% and 90% realised FLOP reduction (tolerance 1.5 points); recovered two full epochs over the remaining training rows under the cell's recovery seed; recalibrated
design.recalibration: BatchNorm running statistics re-estimated on the first 51,200 rows of a seed-2026 permutation of the remaining training rows, weights frozen
design.cells: 2 architectures x 3 families x 5 seeds = 30 teachers, 30 dense references, 120 students

endpoints.unseen_detect: fraction of the held-out family's evaluation rows predicted as any attack class (argmax rule), the primary endpoint
endpoints.unseen_absorption: share of the held-out family's rows predicted as benign and as each remaining attack family (descriptive)
endpoints.unseen_attack_mass: mean of 1 minus the benign probability on the held-out rows (threshold-free, descriptive)
endpoints.in_distribution: recalibrated ground-truth HSR (balanced profile), benign escalation, attack-miss rate, family and fine macro-F1, ECE and per-family recall on the remaining classes
endpoints.paired_gap: dense reference's unseen_detect minus the student's, under the same seed; mean over accepted seeds with a 95% t interval
endpoints.matched: the mean paired difference in in-distribution HSR between student and dense reference is within 0.02

prereg.P1_gap: for an architecture, P1 holds if at 90% realised reduction, for at least two of the three held-out families and for both methods, the paired gap in unseen_detect is at least 0.05 with the lower end of its 95% interval above zero, and the cell is matched in distribution
prereg.S1_dose: descriptive: in the majority of (architecture, family, method) cells the paired gap at 90% exceeds the gap at 70%
prereg.S2_ceiling: descriptive: the dense reference's own unseen_detect per family, the ceiling against which the gap is read

readings.per_architecture: gap_at_matched_risk if P1 holds; gap_but_unmatched if the gap condition holds in at least two families for both methods but matching fails in one of those cells; partial if at least one cell meets the gap condition but P1 fails; no_gap if no cell meets it; a separate flag student_better is set when at least half of the 90% cells have a negative gap with the upper end of the interval below zero
readings.overall: route_open if both architectures read gap_at_matched_risk; route_open_one_architecture if exactly one does; route_closed if both read no_gap; inconclusive otherwise
readings.route_open: pruned detectors miss unseen attack families that the dense detector catches, at matched in-distribution risk, and recovery on training data cannot close it; the method paper targets this gap with a recovery objective that preserves the teacher's behaviour off the training distribution; next is the design of that objective and its baselines, not more measurement
readings.route_open_one_architecture: as route_open, scoped to that architecture, with the other architecture reported as a boundary of the claim
readings.route_closed: compression does not make these detectors forget unseen attack families; the off-distribution method route is closed on this setup, and method effort moves to a problem that is open
readings.inconclusive: the cells are reported as they are; no method is built on a partial result; a targeted follow-up (more seeds or families) is run only if a cell is close to the mark
